96	def get_dxlink_ids(link):
97	    '''
98	    :param link: A DNAnexus link
99	    :type link: dict
100	    :returns: (Object ID, Project ID) if the link is to a data object (or :const:`None`
101	        if no project specified in the link), or (Job ID, Field) if the link is
102	        a job-based object reference (JBOR).
103	    :rtype: tuple
104	
105	    Get the object ID and detail from a link. There are three types of links:
106	
107	    * Simple link of the form ``{"$dnanexus_link": "file-XXXX"}`` returns
108	      ``("file-XXXX", None)``.
109	    * Data object link of the form ``{"$dnanexus_link': {"id": "file-XXXX",
110	      "project": "project-XXXX"}}`` returns ``("file-XXXX", "project-XXXX")``.
111	    * Job-based object reference (JBOR) of the form ``{"$dnanexus_link":
112	      {"job": "job-XXXX", "field": "foo"}}`` returns ``("job-XXXX", "foo")``.
113	    '''
114	    if not is_dxlink(link):
115	        raise DXError('Invalid link: %r' % link)
116	    if isinstance(link['$dnanexus_link'], basestring):
117	        return link['$dnanexus_link'], None
118	    elif 'id' in link['$dnanexus_link']:
119	        return link['$dnanexus_link']['id'], link['$dnanexus_link'].get('project')
120	    else:
121	        return link['$dnanexus_link']['job'], link['$dnanexus_link']['field']

123	def _guess_link_target_type(id_or_link):
124	    # Get the object ID if the input is a link
125	    object_id = get_dxlink_ids(id_or_link)[0] if is_dxlink(id_or_link) else id_or_link
126	    class_name = 'DX' + object_id.split("-", 1)[0].capitalize()
127	    if class_name not in all_bindings:
128	        class_name = {
129	            'DXGlobalworkflow': 'DXGlobalWorkflow'
130	        }.get(class_name)
131	    if class_name not in all_bindings:
132	        raise DXError("Invalid class name: %s", class_name)
133	    cls = all_bindings[class_name]
134	    return cls

136	def get_handler(id_or_link, project=None):
137	    '''
138	    :param id_or_link: String containing an object ID or dict containing a DXLink
139	    :type id_or_link: string or dict
140	    :param project: String project ID to use as the context if the the object is a data object
141	    :type project: string
142	    :rtype: :class:`~dxpy.bindings.DXObject`, :class:`~dxpy.bindings.DXApp`, or :class:`~dxpy.bindings.DXGlobalWorkflow`
143	
144	    Parses a string or DXLink dict. Creates and returns an object handler for it.
145	
146	    Example::
147	
148	        get_handler("file-1234")
149	    '''
150	    try:
151	        cls = _guess_link_target_type(id_or_link)
152	    except Exception as e:
153	        raise DXError("Could not parse link {}: {}".format(id_or_link, e))
154	
155	    if cls in [dxpy.DXApp, dxpy.DXGlobalWorkflow]:
156	        # This special case should translate identifiers of the form
157	        # "app-name" or "app-name/version_or_tag" to the appropriate
158	        # arguments
159	        if dxpy.utils.resolver.is_hashid(id_or_link):
160	            return cls(id_or_link)
161	        else:
162	            slash_pos = id_or_link.find('/')
163	            dash_pos = id_or_link.find('-')
164	            if slash_pos == -1:
165	                return cls(name=id_or_link[dash_pos+1:])
166	            else:
167	                return cls(name=id_or_link[dash_pos+1:slash_pos],
168	                           alias=id_or_link[slash_pos + 1:])
169	    elif project is None or cls in [dxpy.DXJob, dxpy.DXAnalysis, dxpy.DXProject, dxpy.DXContainer]:
170	        # This case is important for the handlers which do not
171	        # take a project field
172	        return cls(id_or_link)
173	    else:
174	        return cls(id_or_link, project=project)
175	
176	def describe(id_or_link, **kwargs):
177	    '''
178	    :param id_or_link: String containing an object ID or dict containing a DXLink,
179	                       or a list of object IDs or dicts containing a DXLink.
180	
181	    Given an object ID, calls :meth:`~dxpy.bindings.DXDataObject.describe` on the object.
182	
183	    Example::
184	
185	        describe("file-1234")
186	
187	    Given a list of object IDs, calls :meth:`~dxpy.api.system_describe_data_objects`.
188	
189	    Example::
190	
191	        describe(["file-1234", "workflow-5678"])
192	
193	    Note: If id_or_link is a list and **kwargs contains a "fields" parameter, these
194	    fields will be returned in the response for each data object in addition to the
195	    fields included by default. Additionally, describe options can be provided for
196	    each data object class in the "classDescribeOptions" kwargs argument. See
197	    https://documentation.dnanexus.com/developer/api/system-methods#api-method-system-describedataobjects
198	    for input parameters used with the multiple object describe method.
199	    '''
200	    # If this is a list, extract the ids.
201	    # TODO: modify the procedure to use project ID when possible
202	    if isinstance(id_or_link, basestring) or is_dxlink(id_or_link):
203	        handler = get_handler(id_or_link)
204	        return handler.describe(**kwargs)
205	    else:
206	        links = []
207	        for link in id_or_link:
208	            # If this entry is a dxlink, then get the id.
209	            if is_dxlink(link):
210	                # Guaranteed by is_dxlink that one of the following will work
211	                if isinstance(link['$dnanexus_link'], basestring):
212	                    link = link['$dnanexus_link']
213	                else:
214	                    link = link['$dnanexus_link']['id']
215	            links.append(link)
216	
217	        # Prepare input to system_describe_data_objects, the same fields will be passed
218	        # for all data object classes; if a class doesn't include a field in its describe
219	        # output, it will be ignored
220	        describe_input = \
221	            dict([(field, True) for field in kwargs['fields']]) if kwargs.get('fields', []) else True
222	        describe_links_input = [{'id': link, 'describe': describe_input} for link in links]
223	        bulk_describe_input = {'objects': describe_links_input}
224	
225	        if 'classDescribeOptions' in kwargs:
226	            bulk_describe_input['classDescribeOptions'] = kwargs['classDescribeOptions']
227	
228	        data_object_descriptions = dxpy.api.system_describe_data_objects(bulk_describe_input)
229	        return [desc['describe'] for desc in data_object_descriptions['results']]
230

4	class ArgsValidator:
5	    """
6	    InputsValidator class. Checks for invalid input combinations set by a JSON schema.
7	
8	    The schema is a dictionary with the following structure:
9	
10	    {
11	    "schema_version": "1.0",
12	    "parser_args":[
13	                  "path"
14	                  "...",
15	                  ]
16	    "condition_1": {
17	        "properties": {
18	            "items": ["path", "json_help"],
19	        },
20	        "condition": "at_least_one_required",
21	        "error_message": {
22	            "message": "..."
23	        },
24	    },
25	    "condition_2": {
26	        "properties": {
27	            "main_key": "path",
28	            "items": ["output","delim"]
29	        },
30	        "condition": "with_at_least_one_required",
31	        "error_message": {
32	            "message": "...",
33	            "type": "warning"
34	            },
35	
36	    """
37	
38	    def __init__(
39	        self,
40	        parser_dict,
41	        schema,
42	        error_handler=print,
43	        warning_handler=print,
44	    ):
45	        self.parser_dict = parser_dict
46	        self.schema = schema
47	        self.error_handler = error_handler
48	        self.warning_handler = warning_handler
49	
50	        self.schema_version = schema.get("schema_version")
51	        self.conditions_funcs = {
52	            "exclusive": "interpret_exclusive",
53	            "exclusive_with_exceptions": "interpret_exclusive_with_exceptions",
54	            "required": "interpret_required",
55	            "at_least_one_required": "interpret_at_least_one_required",
56	            "with_at_least_one_required": "interpret_with_at_least_one_required",
57	            "with_none_of": "interpret_with_none_of",
58	            "mutually_exclusive_group": "interpret_mutually_exclusive_group",
59	        }
60	
61	    ### Schema methods ###
62	    def validate_schema_conditions(self):
63	        # Checking if all conditions exist
64	        present_conditions = [
65	            value.get("condition")
66	            for key, value in self.schema.items()
67	            if key != "schema_version" and key != "parser_args"
68	        ]
69	        not_found = set(present_conditions) - set(self.conditions_funcs)
70	        if len(not_found) != 0:
71	            self.error_handler("{} schema condition is not defined".format(not_found))
72	
73	    ### Checking general methods ###
74	    def interpret_conditions(self):
75	        for key, value in self.schema.items():
76	            if key != "schema_version" and key != "parser_args":
77	                condition = value.get("condition")
78	                method_to_call = self.conditions_funcs.get(condition)
79	                getattr(self, method_to_call)(key)
80	
81	    def throw_schema_message(self, check):
82	        message_type = self.schema.get(check).get("error_message").get("type")
83	        message = self.schema.get(check).get("error_message").get("message")
84	        if message_type == "warning":
85	            self.throw_warning(message)
86	        elif isinstance(message_type, type(None)) or (message_type == "error"):
87	            self.throw_exit_error(message)
88	        else:
89	            self.error_handler(
90	                'Unkown error message in schema: "{}" for key "{}"'.format(type, check)
91	            )
92	
93	    def throw_exit_error(self, message):
94	        self.error_handler(message)
95	
96	    def throw_warning(self, message):
97	        self.warning_handler(message)
98	
99	    def get_parser_values(self, params):
100	        values = [self.parser_dict.get(p) for p in params]
101	        return values
102	
103	    def get_main_key(self, check):
104	        return self.schema.get(check).get("properties").get("main_key")
105	
106	    def get_items(self, check):
107	        return self.schema.get(check).get("properties").get("items")
108	
109	    def get_items_values(self, check):
110	        items = self.get_items(check)
111	        return [self.parser_dict[i] for i in items]
112	
113	    def get_exceptions(self, check):
114	        return self.schema.get(check).get("properties").get("exceptions")
115	
116	    def remove_exceptions_from_list(self, check, list):
117	        exceptions_list = self.get_exceptions(check)
118	        for e in exceptions_list:
119	            list.remove(e)
120	        return list
121	
122	    ### Checking specific methods ###
123	    def interpret_exclusive(self, check):
124	        self.interpret_exclusive_with_exceptions(check, exception_present=False)
125	
126	    def interpret_exclusive_with_exceptions(self, check, exception_present=True):
127	        main_key = self.get_main_key(check)
128	
129	        # Defining args to check and its values
130	        args_to_check = self.schema.get("parser_args")[:]
131	        args_to_check.remove(main_key)
132	        if exception_present:
133	            args_to_check = self.remove_exceptions_from_list(check, args_to_check)
134	        args_to_check_values = self.get_parser_values(args_to_check)
135	
136	        # True check
137	        if self.parser_dict.get(main_key) and any(args_to_check_values):
138	            self.throw_schema_message(check)
139	
140	    def interpret_with_none_of(self, check):
141	        main_key = self.get_main_key(check)
142	        args_to_check_values = self.get_items_values(check)
143	        if self.parser_dict.get(main_key) and any(args_to_check_values):
144	            self.throw_schema_message(check)
145	
146	    def interpret_required(self, check):
147	        self.interpret_at_least_one_required(check)
148	
149	    def interpret_at_least_one_required(self, check, main_key=None):
150	        args_to_check_values = self.get_items_values(check)
151	
152	        if main_key:
153	            if self.parser_dict.get(main_key) and not any(args_to_check_values):
154	                self.throw_schema_message(check)
155	        else:
156	            if not any(args_to_check_values):
157	                self.throw_schema_message(check)
158	
159	    def interpret_with_at_least_one_required(self, check):
160	        main_key = self.get_main_key(check)
161	        self.interpret_at_least_one_required(check, main_key)
162	
163	    def interpret_mutually_exclusive_group(self, check):
164	        args_to_check_values = self.get_items_values(check)
165	        present_args_count = 0
166	
167	        for arg in args_to_check_values:
168	            if arg:
169	                present_args_count += 1
170	
171	        if present_args_count > 1:
172	            self.throw_schema_message(check)
173	
174	    # VALIDATION
175	    def validate_input_combination(self):
176	        self.validate_schema_conditions()
177	        self.interpret_conditions()
178

2	def transform_to_expression_matrix(list_of_dicts):
3	    """
4	    list_of_dicts: list of dictionaries, each of the form
5	    {
6	        "feature_id":<feature_id>,
7	        "sample_id":<sample_id>,
8	        "expression":<expression>
9	    }
10	    Additional key:value pairs are possible, but are not included in the transformed output
11	
12	    How it works:
13	    First, create a dictionary where each key is a sample id, and the values are the feature_id:expression pairs
14	    Then, convert it to a list of dictionaries (the format that output handling is expecting)
15	    Each item in the list is a dictionary containing one "sample_id":sample_id pair, and
16	    multiple feature_id:expression pairs
17	
18	    Returns:
19	    A list of dictionaries, each of the form:
20	    {
21	        "sample_id":<sample_id>,
22	        <feature_id_1>:<expression_1>
23	        <feature_id_2>:<expression_2>
24	        ...
25	        <feature_id_n>:<expression_n>
26	    }
27	    """
28	    transformed_dict = {}
29	    # create a dict of the form
30	    # {
31	    #   <sample_id>:{
32	    #       "sample_id":<sample_id>,
33	    #       <feature_id_1>:<expression_1>,
34	    #       <feature_id_2>:<expression_2>,
35	    #        etc.
36	    #   }
37	    # 
38	    # }
39	    colnames = set()
40	    for entry in list_of_dicts:
41	        # Keep track of all seen feature_ids, they will become the columns of our final table
42	        colnames.add(entry["feature_id"])
43	        if entry["sample_id"] not in transformed_dict:
44	            transformed_dict[entry["sample_id"]] = {"sample_id":entry["sample_id"],entry["feature_id"]:entry["expression"]}
45	        else:
46	            transformed_dict[entry["sample_id"]][entry["feature_id"]] = entry["expression"]
47	    colnames = sorted(list(colnames))
48	    colnames.insert(0,"sample_id")
49	
50	    # We want the output to be a list of dictionaries, rather than a single dicitonary keyed on sample_id
51	    dict_list = list(transformed_dict.values())
52	    for dict_row in dict_list:
53	        for colname in colnames:
54	            if colname not in dict_row:
55	                dict_row[colname] = None
56	
57	    return (dict_list,colnames)

642	    def _wait_on_close(self, timeout=3600*24*1, **kwargs):
643	        elapsed = 0
644	        i = 0
645	        while True:
646	            state = self._get_state(**kwargs)
647	            if state == "closed":
648	                break
649	            if state != "closing":
650	                raise DXError("Unexpected state: " + state)
651	
652	            if elapsed >= timeout or elapsed < 0:
653	                raise DXError("Reached timeout while waiting for the remote object to close")
654	
655	            wait = min(2**7, 2**i)
656	            time.sleep(wait)
657	            i += 1
658	            elapsed += wait

660	    def _wait_until_parts_uploaded(self, timeout=255, **kwargs):
661	        elapsed = 0
662	        i = 0
663	        describe_input = {"fields": {"parts": True, "state": True}}
664	        if self._proj is not None:
665	            describe_input["project"] = self._proj
666	        while True:
667	            describe = self._describe(self._dxid, describe_input, **kwargs)
668	            state, parts = describe["state"], describe["parts"]
669	            if state == "closed" or not parts:
670	                # parts of closed files must have been uploaded successfully
671	                break
672	            else:
673	                is_uploaded = not any(parts[key].get("state", "complete") != "complete" for key in parts)
674	                if is_uploaded:
675	                    break
676	            if elapsed >= timeout or elapsed < 0:
677	                raise DXError("Reached timeout while waiting for parts of the file ({}) to be uploaded".format(self.get_id()))
678	
679	            wait = min(2**7, 2**i)
680	            time.sleep(wait)
681	            i += 1
682	            elapsed += wait

4	class JSONValidator(object):
5	    """
6	    JSON validator class to validate a JSON against a schema.
7	
8	    The schema is a dictionary with the following structure:
9	
10	    {
11	        "key1": {
12	            "type": dict,
13	            "properties": {
14	                "name": {"type": str, "required": True},
15	                "attribute": {"type": str}
16	            }
17	        },
18	        "key2": {
19	            "type": dict,
20	            "properties": {
21	                "xyz": {"type": str},
22	                "abc": {"type": list}
23	            },
24	            "conflicting_keys": [["xyz", "abc"]]
25	        },
26	        "list_key_example": {
27	            "type": list,
28	            "items": {
29	                "type": dict,
30	                "properties": {
31	                    "nested_key1": {"type": str, "required": True},
32	                    "nested_key2": {"type": str}
33	                }
34	            }
35	        },
36	        "id": {
37	            "type": list,
38	        },
39	        "conflicting_keys": [["key1", "key2"]],
40	        "dependent_conditional_keys": {
41	            "list_key_example": ["key1", "key2"]
42	        }
43	    }
44	
45	    Key types can be defined via the "type" key
46	
47	    Required keys can be defined via the "required" key
48	
49	    Conflicting keys can be defined via the "conflicting_keys" key, where the value is a list of lists of keys that are mutually exclusive.
50	    Conflicting keys can be defined at the level of the schema for the entire JSON or at key-level.
51	    In the example above, within "key2" the keys "xyz" and "abc" are mutually exclusive and cannot be present together.
52	    Similarly, at the level of the whole JSON, "key1" and "key2" are mutually exclusive and cannot be present together.
53	
54	    Conditional key combinations can be defined via the dependent_conditional_keys at the level of the schema. These should be defined as a dict where the value is a list.
55	    In the example above, dependent_conditional_keys is defined as {"list_key_example": ["key1", "key2"]}, which means whenever list_key_example is present, either "key1"
56	    or "key2" has to be also present.
57	
58	    Currently the maximum level of nestedness supported for validation is as deep as shown in the example above via the "list_key_example" key.
59	
60	    This is an example of a valid JSON that satisfies all the conditions defined in the schema above:
61	
62	    {
63	        "key1": {
64	            "name": "test",
65	        },
66	        "list_key_example": [
67	            {"nested_key1": "1", "nested_key2": "2"},
68	            {"nested_key1": "3", "nested_key2": "4"},
69	            {"nested_key1": "5"}
70	        ],
71	        "id": ["id_1", "id_2"]
72	    }
73	
74	    """
75	
76	    def __init__(self, schema, error_handler=print):
77	        self.schema = schema
78	        self.error_handler = error_handler
79	
80	        if not isinstance(schema, dict) or not schema:
81	            error_handler("Schema must be a non-empty dict.")
82	
83	    def validate(self, input_json):
84	        if not isinstance(input_json, dict) or not input_json:
85	            self.error_handler("Input JSON must be a non-empty dict.")
86	
87	        self.error_on_invalid_keys(input_json)
88	
89	        self.validate_types(input_json)
90	
91	        for key, value in self.schema.items():
92	            if key in input_json:
93	                self.validate_properties(value.get("properties", {}), input_json[key])
94	
95	                if value.get("type") == list:
96	                    self.validate_list_items(
97	                        value.get("items", {}), input_json[key], key
98	                    )
99	
100	                # Check for incompatible/conflicting subkeys defined at the key-level
101	                if value.get("conflicting_keys"):
102	                    self.check_incompatible_subkeys(input_json, key)
103	                    self.check_incompatible_subkeys(input_json[key], key)
104	
105	
106	        self.check_incompatible_keys(input_json)
107	        self.check_dependent_key_combinations(input_json)
108	
109	    def validate_types(self, input_dict):
110	        for key, value in input_dict.items():
111	            if not isinstance(value, self.schema.get(key, {}).get("type")):
112	                self.error_handler(
113	                    "Key '{}' has an invalid type. Expected {} but got {}".format(
114	                        key, self.schema.get(key, {}).get("type"), type(value)
115	                    )
116	                )
117	
118	    def validate_properties(self, properties, input_dict):
119	        for key, value in properties.items():
120	            if key not in input_dict and value.get("required"):
121	                self.error_handler(
122	                    "Required key '{}' was not found in the input JSON.".format(key)
123	                )
124	            if key in input_dict and not isinstance(input_dict[key], value.get("type")):
125	                self.error_handler(
126	                    "Key '{}' has an invalid type. Expected {} but got {}".format(
127	                        key, value.get("type"), type(input_dict[key])
128	                    )
129	                )
130	
131	    def validate_list_items(self, item_schema, input_list, key_name):
132	        item_type = item_schema.get("type")
133	        if item_type:
134	            for item in input_list:
135	                if not isinstance(item, item_type):
136	                    self.error_handler(
137	                        "Expected list items within '{}' to be of type {} but got {} instead.".format(
138	                            key_name, item_type, type(item)
139	                        )
140	                    )
141	                self.validate_properties(item_schema.get("properties", {}), item)
142	        else:
143	            if not isinstance(input_list, list):
144	                self.error_handler(
145	                    "Expected list but got {} for {}".format(type(input_list), key_name)
146	                )
147	            for item in input_list:
148	                if not isinstance(item, str):
149	                    self.error_handler(
150	                        "Expected list items to be of type string for {}.".format(
151	                            key_name
152	                        )
153	                    )
154	
155	    def check_incompatible_subkeys(self, input_json, current_key):
156	        for keys in self.schema.get(current_key, {}).get("conflicting_keys", []):
157	            if all(k in input_json for k in keys):
158	                self.error_handler(
159	                    "For {}, exactly one of {} must be provided in the supplied JSON object.".format(
160	                        current_key, " or ".join(keys)
161	                    )
162	                )
163	
164	    def check_incompatible_keys(self, input_json):
165	        for keys in self.schema.get("conflicting_keys", []):
166	            if all(key in input_json for key in keys):
167	                self.error_handler(
168	                    "Exactly one of {} must be provided in the supplied JSON object.".format(
169	                        " or ".join(keys)
170	                    )
171	                )
172	
173	    def check_dependent_key_combinations(
174	        self, input_json, enforce_one_associated_key=False
175	    ):
176	        mandatory_combinations = self.schema.get("dependent_conditional_keys", {})
177	        for main_key, associated_keys in mandatory_combinations.items():
178	            if main_key in input_json:
179	                present_associated_keys = [
180	                    key for key in associated_keys if key in input_json
181	                ]
182	                if len(present_associated_keys) == 0:
183	                    self.error_handler(
184	                        "When {} is present, one of the following keys must be also present: {}.".format(
185	                            main_key, ", ".join(associated_keys)
186	                        )
187	                    )
188	                if len(present_associated_keys) > 1 and enforce_one_associated_key:
189	                    self.error_handler(
190	                        "Only one of the associated keys {} can be present for main key {}".format(
191	                            ", ".join(associated_keys)
192	                        )
193	                    )
194	
195	    def error_on_invalid_keys(self, input_json):
196	        invalid_keys = []
197	        for key in input_json:
198	            if key not in self.schema:
199	                invalid_keys.append(key)
200	
201	        if invalid_keys:
202	            self.error_handler(
203	                "Found following invalid filters: {}".format(invalid_keys)
204	            )
205	
206	    def are_list_items_within_range(
207	        self,
208	        input_json,
209	        key,
210	        start_subkey,
211	        end_subkey,
212	        window_width=250000000,
213	        check_each_separately=False,
214	    ):
215	        """
216	        This won't run by default when calling .validate() on a JSONValidator object. Run it separately when necessary
217	        """
218	
219	        for item in input_json[key]:
220	            if int(item[end_subkey]) <= int(item[start_subkey]):
221	                self.error_handler(
222	                    "{} cannot be less than or equal to the {}".format(
223	                        end_subkey, start_subkey
224	                    )
225	                )
226	
227	            if check_each_separately:
228	                if item[end_subkey] - item[start_subkey] > window_width:
229	                    self.error_handler(
230	                        "Range of {} and {} cannot be greater than {} for each item in {}".format(
231	                            start_subkey, end_subkey, window_width, key
232	                        )
233	                    )
234	        if not check_each_separately:
235	            # Check will be done across all items in the list
236	            # the entire search would be limited to window_width
237	            start_values = [int(item[start_subkey]) for item in input_json[key]]
238	            end_values = [int(item[end_subkey]) for item in input_json[key]]
239	
240	            if max(end_values) - min(start_values) > window_width:
241	                self.error_handler(
242	                    "Range cannot be greater than {} for {}".format(window_width, key)
243	                )

14	            )
15	            if "error" in response:
16	                if response["error"]["type"] == "InvalidInput":

18	                        "Insufficient permissions due to the project policy.\n"
19	                        + response["error"]["message"]
20	                    )
21	                elif response["error"]["type"] == "QueryTimeOut":
22	                    err_message = "Please consider using --sql option to generate the SQL query and execute query via a private compute cluster."
23	                elif response["error"]["type"] == "DataTooLarge":
24	                    err_message = "Please consider using --sql option to generate the SQL query and execute query via a private compute cluster."
25	                else:

27	                self.error_handler(str(err_message))

32	    def get_data(self, payload, record_id):

86	def get_folder_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj, folderpath):
87	    '''
88	    :param text: String to be tab-completed; still in escaped form
89	    :type text: string
90	    :param delim_pos: index of last unescaped "/" in text
91	    :type delim_pos: int
92	    :param dxproj: DXProject handler to use
93	    :type dxproj: DXProject
94	    :param folderpath: Unescaped path in which to search for folder matches
95	    :type folderpath: string
96	    :returns: List of matches
97	    :rtype: list of strings
98	
99	    Members of the returned list are guaranteed to start with *text*
100	    and be in escaped form for consumption by the command-line.
101	    '''
102	    try:
103	        folders = dxproj.list_folder(folder=folderpath, only='folders')['folders']
104	        folder_names = [name[name.rfind('/') + 1:] for name in folders]
105	        if text != '' and delim_pos != len(text) - 1:
106	            folder_names += ['.', '..']
107	        prefix = text[:delim_pos + 1]
108	        return [prefix + f + '/' for f in folder_names if (prefix + f + '/').startswith(text)]
109	    except:
110	        return []

158	def path_completer(text, expected=None, classes=None, perm_level=None,
159	                   include_current_proj=False, typespec=None, visibility=None):
160	    '''
161	    :param text: String to tab-complete to a path matching the syntax project-name:folder/entity_or_folder_name
162	    :type text: string
163	    :param expected: "folder", "entity", "project", or None (no restriction) as to the types of answers to look for
164	    :type expected: string
165	    :param classes: if expected="entity", the possible data object classes that are acceptable
166	    :type classes: list of strings
167	    :param perm_level: the minimum permissions level required, e.g. "VIEW" or "CONTRIBUTE"
168	    :type perm_level: string
169	    :param include_current_proj: Indicate whether the current project's name should be a potential result
170	    :type include_current_proj: boolean
171	    :param visibility: Visibility with which to restrict the completion (one of "either", "visible", or "hidden") (default behavior is dependent on *text*)
172	
173	    Returns a list of matches to the text and restricted by the
174	    requested parameters.
175	    '''
176	    colon_pos = get_last_pos_of_char(':', text)
177	    slash_pos = get_last_pos_of_char('/', text)
178	    delim_pos = max(colon_pos, slash_pos)
179	
180	    # First get projects if necessary
181	    matches = []
182	    if expected == 'project' and colon_pos > 0 and colon_pos == len(text) - 1:
183	        if dxpy.find_one_project(zero_ok=True, name=text[:colon_pos]) is not None:
184	            return [text + " "]
185	
186	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos < 0:
187	        # Might be tab-completing a project, but don't ever include
188	        # whatever's set as dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID unless expected == "project"
189	        # Also, don't bother if text=="" and expected is NOT "project"
190	        # Also, add space if expected == "project"
191	        if text != "" or expected == 'project':
192	            results = dxpy.find_projects(describe=True, level=perm_level)
193	            if not include_current_proj:
194	                results = [r for r in results if r['id'] != dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID]
195	            matches += [escape_colon(r['describe']['name'])+':' for r in results if r['describe']['name'].startswith(text)]
196	
197	    if expected == 'project':
198	        return matches
199	
200	    # Attempt to tab-complete to a folder or data object name
201	    if colon_pos < 0 and slash_pos >= 0:
202	        # Not tab-completing a project, and the project is unambiguous
203	        # (use dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
204	        if dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is not None:
205	            # try-catch block in case dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID is garbage
206	            try:
207	                dxproj = dxpy.get_handler(dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
208	                folderpath, entity_name = clean_folder_path(text)
209	                matches += get_folder_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj, folderpath)
210	                if expected != 'folder':
211	                    if classes is not None:
212	                        for classname in classes:
213	                            matches += get_data_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj,
214	                                                        folderpath, classname=classname,
215	                                                        typespec=typespec,
216	                                                        visibility=visibility)
217	                    else:
218	                        matches += get_data_matches(text, slash_pos, dxproj,
219	                                                    folderpath, typespec=typespec,
220	                                                    visibility=visibility)
221	            except:
222	                pass
223	    else:
224	        # project is given by a path, but attempt to resolve to an
225	        # object or folder anyway
226	        try:
227	            proj_ids, folderpath, entity_name = resolve_path(text, multi_projects=True)
228	        except ResolutionError as details:
229	            sys.stderr.write("\n" + fill(str(details)))
230	            return matches
231	        for proj in proj_ids:
232	            # protects against dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID being garbage
233	            try:
234	                dxproj = dxpy.get_handler(proj)
235	                matches += get_folder_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj, folderpath)
236	                if expected != 'folder':
237	                    if classes is not None:
238	                        for classname in classes:
239	                            matches += get_data_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj,
240	                                                        folderpath, classname=classname,
241	                                                        typespec=typespec, visibility=visibility)
242	                    else:
243	                        matches += get_data_matches(text, delim_pos, dxproj,
244	                                                    folderpath, typespec=typespec,
245	                                                    visibility=visibility)
246	            except:
247	                pass
248	    return matches

107	def _get_destination_project(json_spec, args, build_project_id=None):
108	    """
109	    Returns destination project in which the workflow should be created.
110	    In can be set in multiple ways whose order of precedence is:
111	    1. --destination, -d option supplied with `dx build`,
112	    2. 'project' specified in the json file,
113	    3. project set in the dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID environment variable.
114	    """
115	    if build_project_id:
116	        return build_project_id
117	    if 'project' in json_spec:
118	        return json_spec['project']
119	    if dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID:
120	        return dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID
121	    error_msg = "Can't create a workflow without specifying a destination project; "
122	    error_msg += "please use the -d/--destination flag to explicitly specify a project"

175	def _version_exists(json_spec, name=None, version=None):
176	    """
177	    Returns True if a global workflow with the given name and version
178	    already exists in the platform and the user has developer rights
179	    to the workflow. "name" and "version" can be passed if we already
180	    made a "describe" API call on the global workflow and so know the
181	    requested name and version already exists.
182	    """
183	    try: 
184	        requested_name = json_spec['name']
185	        requested_version = json_spec['version']
186	    except:
187	        raise WorkflowBuilderException("Both 'name' and 'version' fields must be given in the dxworkflow.json/source workflow spec to build/update a global workflow.")
188	
189	    if requested_name == name and requested_version == version:
190	        return True
191	    else:
192	        try:
193	            desc_output = dxpy.api.global_workflow_describe('globalworkflow-' + json_spec['name'],
194	                                                            alias=json_spec['version'],
195	                                                            input_params={"fields": {"name": True,
196	                                                                                     "version": True}})
197	            return desc_output['name'] == json_spec['name'] and desc_output['version'] == json_spec['version']
198	        except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError:
199	            return False
200	        except:
201	            raise

204	def _get_validated_stage(stage, stage_index):
205	    # required keys
206	    if 'executable' not in stage:
207	        raise WorkflowBuilderException(
208	            "executable is not specified for stage with index {}".format(stage_index))
209	
210	    # print ignored keys if present in json_spec
211	    supported_keys = {"id", "input", "executable", "name", "folder",
212	                      "executionPolicy", "systemRequirements"}
213	    unsupported_keys = _get_unsupported_keys(stage.keys(), supported_keys)
214	    if len(unsupported_keys) > 0:
215	        print("Warning: the following stage fields are not supported and will be ignored: {}"
216	              .format(", ".join(unsupported_keys)))
217	
218	    return stage

221	def validate_ignore_reuse(stages, ignore_reuse_stages):
222	    """
223	    Checks if each stage ID specified in ignore_reuse_stages exists in
224	    the workflow definition. If ignore_reuse_stages contains
225	    only '*', the field is valid.
226	    """
227	    if not isinstance(ignore_reuse_stages, list):
228	         raise WorkflowBuilderException('"IgnoreReuse must be a list of strings - stage IDs or "*"')
229	
230	    ignore_reuse_set = set(ignore_reuse_stages)
231	    if '*' in ignore_reuse_set and len(ignore_reuse_set) == 1:
232	        return
233	
234	    stage_ids = set([stage.get('id') for stage in stages])
235	    for ignored in ignore_reuse_set:
236	        if ignored not in stage_ids:
237	            raise WorkflowBuilderException(
238	                'Stage with ID {} not found. Add a matching "id" for the stage you wish to set ignoreReuse for'.format(ignored))

242	    """

246	        raise WorkflowBuilderException("Stages must be specified as a list of dictionaries")

271	def _validate_json_for_global_workflow(json_spec, args):
272	    """
273	    Validates fields used for building a global workflow.
274	    Since building a global workflow is done after all the underlying workflows
275	    are built, which may be time-consuming, we validate as much as possible here.
276	    """
277	    if 'name' not in json_spec:
278	        raise WorkflowBuilderException(
279	            "dxworkflow.json/source workflow spec contains no 'name' field, but it is required to build a global workflow")
280	    if not dxpy.executable_builder.GLOBAL_EXEC_NAME_RE.match(json_spec['name']):
281	        raise WorkflowBuilderException(
282	            "The name of your workflow must match /^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+$/")
283	    if json_spec['name'] != json_spec['name'].lower():
284	        logger.warn('workflow name "{}" should be all lowercase'.format(json_spec['name']))
285	
286	    if 'version' not in json_spec:
287	        raise WorkflowBuilderException(
288	            "dxworkflow.json/source workflow spec contains no 'version' field, but it is required to build a global workflow")
289	    if not dxpy.executable_builder.GLOBAL_EXEC_VERSION_RE.match(json_spec['version']):
290	        logger.warn('"version" {} should be semver compliant (e.g. of the form X.Y.Z)'.format(json_spec['version']))
291	
292	    if 'details' in json_spec:
293	        if not isinstance(json_spec['details'], dict):
294	            raise WorkflowBuilderException(
295	                'The field "details" must be a dictionary')
296	
297	    if 'regionalOptions' in json_spec:
298	        if not (isinstance(json_spec['regionalOptions'], dict)
299	                and json_spec['regionalOptions']
300	                and all([isinstance(i, dict) for i in json_spec['regionalOptions'].values()])):
301	            raise WorkflowBuilderException(
302	                'The field "regionalOptions" must be a non-empty dictionary whose values are dictionaries')

306	def _get_validated_json(json_spec, args):
307	    """
308	    Validates workflow spec and returns the json that can be sent with the
309	    /workflow/new API or /globalworkflow/new request.
310	    """
311	    if not json_spec:
312	        return
313	    if not args:
314	        return
315	
316	    validated_spec = copy.deepcopy(json_spec)
317	
318	    # print ignored keys if present in json_spec
319	    unsupported_keys = _get_unsupported_keys(validated_spec.keys(), SUPPORTED_KEYS)
320	    if len(unsupported_keys) > 0:
321	        logger.warn(
322	            "Warning: the following root level fields are not supported and will be ignored: {}"
323	                .format(", ".join(unsupported_keys)))
324	
325	
326	    if 'stages' in validated_spec:
327	        validated_spec['stages'] = _get_validated_stages(validated_spec['stages'])
328	
329	    if 'name' in validated_spec and not args._from:
330	        dir_name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(args.src_dir))
331	        if dir_name != validated_spec['name']:
332	            logger.warn(
333	                'workflow name "{}" does not match containing directory "{}"'.format(validated_spec['name'], dir_name))
334	
335	    if 'ignoreReuse' in validated_spec:
336	        validate_ignore_reuse(validated_spec['stages'], validated_spec['ignoreReuse'])
337	
338	    validated_documentation_fields = _get_validated_json_for_build_or_update(validated_spec, args)
339	    validated_spec.update(validated_documentation_fields)
340	
341	    # Project-based workflow specific validation
342	    if args.mode == 'workflow':
343	        validated = _validate_json_for_regular_workflow(json_spec, args)
344	        validated_spec.update(validated)
345

376	def _assert_executable_regions_match(workflow_enabled_regions, workflow_spec):
377	    """
378	    Check if the dependent apps/applets/subworkflows in the workflow are enabled in requested regions
379	    Returns the subset of requested regions where all the dependent executables are enabled
380	    If the workflow contains any applets, then the workflow can be currently enabled
381	    in only one region - the region in which the applets are stored.
382	    """
383	    if not workflow_enabled_regions: # empty set
384	        return workflow_enabled_regions
385	    
386	    # get executable from all stages and sort them in the order app/applet/globalworkflow/workflow
387	    executables = sorted([i.get("executable") for i in workflow_spec.get("stages")])
388	
389	    for exect in executables:
390	        if exect.startswith("applet-"):
391	            applet_project = dxpy.DXApplet(exect).project
392	            applet_region = dxpy.DXProject(applet_project).region
393	            if {applet_region} != workflow_enabled_regions:                
394	                raise WorkflowBuilderException("The applet {} is not available in all requested region(s) {}"
395	                                               .format(exect, ','.join(workflow_enabled_regions)))
396	
397	        elif exect.startswith("app-"):
398	            app_regional_options = dxpy.api.app_describe(exect, input_params={"fields": {"regionalOptions": True}})
399	            app_regions = set(app_regional_options['regionalOptions'].keys())
400	            if not workflow_enabled_regions.issubset(app_regions):
401	                additional_workflow_regions = workflow_enabled_regions.difference(app_regions)
402	                mesg = "The app {} is enabled in regions {} while the global workflow in {}.".format(
403	                    exect, ", ".join(app_regions), ", ".join(workflow_enabled_regions))
404	                mesg += " The workflow will not be able to run in {}.".format(", ".join(additional_workflow_regions))
405	                mesg += " If you are a developer of the app, you can enable the app in {} to run the workflow in that region(s).".format(
406	                    ", ".join(additional_workflow_regions))
407	                logger.warn(mesg)
408	                workflow_enabled_regions.intersection_update(app_regions)
409	
410	        elif exect.startswith("workflow-"):
411	             # We recurse to check the regions of the executables of the inner workflow
412	            inner_workflow_spec = dxpy.api.workflow_describe(exect)
413	            workflow_enabled_regions = _assert_executable_regions_match(workflow_enabled_regions, inner_workflow_spec)
414	
415	        elif exect.startswith("globalworkflow-"):
416	            raise WorkflowBuilderException("Building a global workflow with nested global workflows is not yet supported")
417	
418	    return workflow_enabled_regions

430	def _get_validated_enabled_regions(json_spec, args):
431	    """
432	    Returns a set of regions (region names) in which the global workflow
433	    should be enabled. 
434	    
435	    1. validates and synchronizes the regions passed via CLI argument and in the regionalOptions field.
436	    2. checks if these regions are included in the permitted regions of the bill_to
437	    3. checks if the dependencies in all the stages are enabled in these regions
438	    """
439	    # Determine in which regions the global workflow are requested to be available
440	    enabled_regions = dxpy.executable_builder.get_enabled_regions('globalworkflow',
441	                                                                  json_spec,
442	                                                                  args.region,
443	                                                                  WorkflowBuilderException)
444	    if not enabled_regions:
445	        enabled_regions = []
446	        if not dxpy.PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID:
447	            msg = "A context project must be selected to enable a workflow in the project's region."
448	            msg += " You can use 'dx select' to select a project. Otherwise you can use --region option"
449	            msg += " to select a region in which the workflow should be enabled"
450	            raise(WorkflowBuilderException(msg))
451	        current_selected_region = dxpy.api.project_describe(dxpy.PROJECT_CONTEXT_ID,
452	                                           input_params={"fields": {"region": True}})["region"]
453	
454	        enabled_regions.append(current_selected_region)
455	
456	    # Get billable regions
457	    enabled_regions = set(enabled_regions)
458	    billable_regions = dxpy.executable_builder.get_permitted_regions(
459	        json_spec["billTo"], WorkflowBuilderException)
460	    if not enabled_regions.issubset(billable_regions):
461	        raise WorkflowBuilderException("The global workflow cannot be enabled in regions {}, which are not among the permittedRegions of the billTo."
462	                                       .format(",".join(enabled_regions.difference(billable_regions))))
463	
464	    # Verify dependencies in all the stages are also enabled in these regions
465	    enabled_regions = _assert_executable_regions_match(enabled_regions, json_spec)
466	    
467	    if not enabled_regions:
468	        raise AssertionError("This workflow should be enabled in at least one region.")
469	
470	    return enabled_regions

473	def _create_temporary_projects(enabled_regions, bill_to):
474	    """
475	    Creates a temporary project needed to build an underlying workflow
476	    for a global workflow. Returns a dictionary with region names as keys
477	    and project IDs as values
478	
479	    The regions in which projects will be created can be:
480	    i. regions specified in the dxworkflow.json/source workflow spec "regionalOptions"
481	    ii. regions specified as the argument "--region" when calling "dx build"
482	    iii. current context project, if none of the above are set
483	    iv. the regions where dependent applets/apps/workflows are enabled
484	    """
485	    # Create one temp project in each region
486	    projects_by_region = {}  # Project IDs by region
487	    for region in enabled_regions:
488	        try:
489	            project_input = {"name": "Temporary build project for dx build global workflow",
490	                             "region": region,
491	                             "billTo": bill_to}
492	            temp_project = dxpy.api.project_new(project_input)["id"]
493	            projects_by_region[region] = temp_project
494	            logger.debug("Created temporary project {} to build in".format(temp_project))
495	        except:
496	            # Clean up any temp projects that might have been created
497	            if projects_by_region:
498	                dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())
499	            err_exit()
500	    return projects_by_region

504	    """
505	    Creates a workflow in a temporary project for each enabled region.
506	    Returns a tuple of dictionaries: workflow IDs by region and project IDs by region.
507	    The caller is responsible for destroying the projects if this method returns properly.
508	    """
509	    projects_by_region = _create_temporary_projects(enabled_regions, json_spec["billTo"])
510	    workflows_by_region = {}

521	    except:
522	        # Clean up
523	        if projects_by_region:
524	            dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())

530	def _build_global_workflow(json_spec, enabled_regions, args):
531	    """
532	    Creates a workflow in a temporary project for each enabled region
533	    and builds a global workflow on the platform based on these workflows.
534	    """
535	    workflows_by_region, projects_by_region = {}, {}  # IDs by region
536	    try:
537	        # prepare "regionalOptions" field for the globalworkflow/new input
538	        existing_regional_options = json_spec.get('regionalOptions', {})
539	
540	        if existing_regional_options:
541	            if set(existing_regional_options.keys()) != set(enabled_regions):
542	                raise WorkflowBuilderException("These enabled regions do have regional options specified \
543	                                           in the JSON spec or from --extra-args: {}",
544	                                           ",".join(set(enabled_regions).difference(set(existing_regional_options.keys()))))
545	                
546	            updated_regional_options= copy.deepcopy(existing_regional_options)
547	        else:
548	            updated_regional_options = dict.fromkeys(enabled_regions, {})
549	        
550	        workflows_by_region, projects_by_region = \
551	            _build_underlying_workflows(enabled_regions, json_spec, args)
552	        for region, workflow_id in workflows_by_region.items():
553	            updated_regional_options[region]["workflow"] = workflow_id
554	
555	        # update existing regionalOptions with underlying workflow ids and ignore regions that are not enabled
556	        json_spec.update({'regionalOptions': updated_regional_options})
557	
558	        # leave only fields that are actually used to build the workflow
559	        gwf_provided_keys = GLOBALWF_SUPPORTED_KEYS.intersection(set(json_spec.keys()))
560	        gwf_final_json = dict((k, v) for k, v in json_spec.items() if k in gwf_provided_keys)
561	
562	        # we don't want to print the whole documentation to the screen so we'll remove these fields
563	        print_spec = copy.deepcopy(gwf_final_json)
564	        if "description" in gwf_final_json:
565	            del print_spec["description"]
566	        if "developerNotes" in gwf_final_json:
567	            del print_spec["developerNotes"]
568	        logger.info("Will create global workflow with spec: {}".format(json.dumps(print_spec)))
569	
570	        # Create a new global workflow version on the platform
571	        global_workflow_id = dxpy.api.global_workflow_new(gwf_final_json)["id"]
572	
573	        logger.info("Uploaded global workflow {n}/{v} successfully".format(n=gwf_final_json["name"],
574	                                                                           v=gwf_final_json["version"]))
575	        logger.info("You can publish this workflow with:")
576	        logger.info("  dx publish {n}/{v}".format(n=gwf_final_json["name"],
577	                                                  v=gwf_final_json["version"]))
578	    finally:
579	        # Clean up
580	        if projects_by_region:
581	            dxpy.executable_builder.delete_temporary_projects(projects_by_region.values())
582	
583	    # Set any additional fields on the created workflow
584	    try:
585	        _set_categories_on_workflow(global_workflow_id, gwf_final_json.get("categories", []))
586	    except:
587	        logger.warn(
588	            "The workflow {n}/{v} was created but setting categories failed".format(n=gwf_final_json['name'],
589	                                                                                    v=gwf_final_json['version']))
590	        raise
591	
592	    return global_workflow_id

639	def _build_or_update_workflow(args, parser):
640	    """
641	    Creates or updates a workflow on the platform.
642	    Returns the workflow ID, or None if the workflow cannot be created.
643	    """
644	    try:
645	        if args.mode == 'workflow':
646	            json_spec = _fetch_spec_from_dxworkflowjson(args.src_dir, "dxworkflow.json", parser)
647	            json_spec.update(args.extra_args or {})
648	            json_spec = _get_validated_json(json_spec, args)
649	            workflow_id = _build_regular_workflow(json_spec, args.keep_open)
650	        elif args.mode == 'globalworkflow':
651	            if args._from:
652	                json_spec = args._from
653	            else:
654	                json_spec = _fetch_spec_from_dxworkflowjson(args.src_dir, "dxworkflow.json", parser)
655	            
656	            # Override version number in json_spec if --version is specified
657	            # version is required when building global workflow but is optional for workflow
658	            # so `dx build` requires --version to be specified when using the --from
659	            if args.version_override:
660	                json_spec["version"] = args.version_override
661	
662	            json_spec.update(args.extra_args or {})
663	            json_spec = _get_validated_json(json_spec, args)
664	            
665	            # Check if the local or source workflow is compiled by dxCompiler that supported dependency annotation
666	            if json_spec.get("tags") and "dxCompiler" in json_spec["tags"]:
667	                _check_dxcompiler_version(json_spec)
668	                if not args.brief:
669	                    _notify_instance_type_selection(json_spec)
670	                    _notify_dependencies(json_spec)
671	            
672	            json_spec = _cleanup_empty_keys(json_spec)
673	            # Verify if the global workflow already exists and if the user has developer rights to it
674	            # If the global workflow name doesn't exist, the user is free to build it
675	            # If the name does exist two things can be done:
676	            # * either update the requested version, if this version already exists
677	            # * or create the version if it doesn't exist
678	            existing_workflow = dxpy.executable_builder.verify_developer_rights('globalworkflow-' + json_spec['name'])
679	            if existing_workflow and _version_exists(json_spec,
680	                                                     existing_workflow.name,
681	                                                     existing_workflow.version):
682	                workflow_id = _update_global_workflow(json_spec, args, existing_workflow.id)
683	            else:
684	                json_spec["billTo"] = dxpy.executable_builder.get_valid_bill_to(args.bill_to, WorkflowBuilderException)
685	                enabled_regions = _get_validated_enabled_regions(json_spec, args)
686	                workflow_id = _build_global_workflow(json_spec, enabled_regions, args)
687	        else:
688	            raise WorkflowBuilderException("Unrecognized workflow type: {}".format(args.mode))
689	    except dxpy.exceptions.DXAPIError as e:
690	        raise e
691	    return workflow_id

55	def run(function_name=None, function_input=None):
56	    """Triggers the execution environment entry point processor.
57	
58	    Use this function in the program entry point code:
59	
60	    .. code-block:: python
61	
62	       import dxpy
63	
64	       @dxpy.entry_point('main')
65	       def hello(i):
66	           pass
67	
68	       dxpy.run()
69	
70	    This method may be used to invoke the program either in a production
71	    environment (inside the execution environment) or for local
72	    debugging (in the debug harness), as follows:
73	
74	    If the environment variable *DX_JOB_ID* is set, the processor
75	    retrieves the job with that ID from the API server. The job's
76	    *function* field indicates the function name to be invoked. That
77	    function name is looked up in the table of all methods decorated
78	    with *@dxpy.entry_point('name')* in the module from which
79	    :func:`run()` was called, and the matching method is invoked (with
80	    the job's input supplied as parameters). This is the mode of
81	    operation used in the DNAnexus execution environment.
82	
83	    .. warning::
84	
85	       The parameters *function_name* and *function_input* are
86	       disregarded in this mode of operation.
87	
88	    If the environment variable *DX_JOB_ID* is not set, the function
89	    name may be given in *function_name*; if not set, it is set by the
90	    environment variable *DX_TEST_FUNCTION*. The function input may be
91	    given in *function_input*; if not set, it is set by the local file
92	    *job_input.json* which is expected to be present.
93	
94	    The absence of *DX_JOB_ID* signals to :func:`run()` that execution
95	    is happening in the debug harness. In this mode of operation, all
96	    calls to :func:`dxpy.bindings.dxjob.new_dxjob()` (and higher level
97	    handler methods which use it) are intercepted, and :func:`run()` is
98	    invoked instead with appropriate inputs.
99	
100	    """
101	
102	    global RUN_COUNT
103	    RUN_COUNT += 1
104	
105	    dx_working_dir = os.getcwd()
106	
107	    if dxpy.JOB_ID is not None:
108	        logging.basicConfig()
109	
110	        try:
111	            logging.getLogger().addHandler(dxpy.DXLogHandler())
112	        except dxpy.exceptions.DXError:
113	            print("TODO: FIXME: the EE client should die if logging is not available")
114	
115	        job = dxpy.describe(dxpy.JOB_ID)
116	    else:
117	        if function_name is None:
118	            function_name = os.environ.get('DX_TEST_FUNCTION', 'main')
119	        if function_input is None:
120	            with open("job_input.json", "r") as fh:
121	                function_input = json.load(fh)
122	
123	        job = {'function': function_name, 'input': function_input}
124	
125	    with open("job_error_reserved_space", "w") as fh:
126	        fh.write("This file contains reserved space for writing job errors in case the filesystem becomes full.\n" + " "*1024*64)
127	
128	    print("Invoking", job.get('function'), "with", job.get('input'))
129	
130	    try:
131	        result = ENTRY_POINT_TABLE[job['function']](**job['input'])
132	    except dxpy.AppError as e:
133	        save_error(e, dx_working_dir, error_type="AppError")
134	        raise
135	    except Exception as e:
136	        save_error(e, dx_working_dir)
137	        raise
138	
139	    if result is not None:
140	        # TODO: protect against client removing its original working directory
141	        os.chdir(dx_working_dir)
142	        with open("job_output.json", "w") as fh:
143	                json.dump(result, fh, indent=2, cls=DXJSONEncoder)
144	                fh.write("\n")
145	
146	    return result

176	        if ispec.get("type") == "int":
177	            kwargs["type"] = int
178	        elif ispec.get("type") == "float":
179	            kwargs["type"] = float
180	        elif ispec.get("type") == "boolean":
181	            kwargs["type"] = bool
182	        elif ispec.get("type") != "string":
183	            json_inputs.add(ispec["name"])
184	
185	        if ispec.get("optional") != None:
186	            kwargs["required"] = not ispec["optional"]
187	
188	        parser.add_argument("--" + ispec["name"], **kwargs)
189	
190	    inputs = {}
191	    for i, value in vars(parser.parse_args(args)).items():
192	        if value is None:
193	            continue
194	        if i in json_inputs:
195	            try:
196	                inputs[i] = json.loads(value)
197	            except ValueError:
198	                from dxpy.utils.resolver import resolve_existing_path
199	                project, path, results = resolve_existing_path(value, ask_to_resolve=False, describe={'id': True}, allow_mult=False)
200	                print(project, path, results)
201	                if results is None or len(results) != 1:
202	                    raise ValueError("Value {v} could not be resolved".format(v=value))
203	                inputs[i] = dxpy.dxlink(results[0]['id'], project_id=project)
204	        else:
205	            inputs[i] = value
206	
207	    return inputs

209	def entry_point(entry_point_name):

212	    Example:

214	    .. code-block:: python
215	
216	       @dxpy.entry_point('main')
217	       def hello(i):
218	           pass
219	
220	    """
221	    def wrap(f):
222	        ENTRY_POINT_TABLE[entry_point_name] = f
223	        @wraps(f)
224	        def wrapped_f(*args, **kwargs):
225	            return f(*args, **kwargs)
226	        return wrapped_f

242	class DXExecDependencyInstaller(object):
243	    """
244	    Installs dependencies specified by the job.
245	
246	    Dependencies are processed in the order specified in the
247	    bundledDepends, execDepends, and dependencies arrays of the
248	    runSpec hash (the former two are deprecated). Neighboring package
249	    dependencies of the same type are grouped.
250	    """
251	    group_pms = ("apt", "gem", "cpan", "cran", "pip", "pip3")
252	
253	    def __init__(self, executable_desc, job_desc, logger=None):
254	        """
255	        :param executable_desc: The description of the executable of
256	            this job, which can be obtained in the response of the
257	            /executable-x/describe request. This dict must contain the
258	            following keys:
259	                - "runSpec"
260	        :type executable_desc: dict
261	        :param job_desc: The description of this job, which can be
262	            obtained in the response of the /job-x/describe request.
263	            If ``executable_desc["runSpec"]`` has key
264	            "bundledDependsByRegion", then this dict must contain the
265	            following keys:
266	                - "region"
267	        :type job_desc: dict
268	        """
269	        if "runSpec" not in executable_desc:
270	            raise DXExecDependencyError('Expected field "runSpec" to be present in executable description"')
271	
272	        if "bundledDependsByRegion" in executable_desc["runSpec"] and "region" not in job_desc:
273	            raise DXExecDependencyError("Expected key 'region' in job description")
274	
275	        self.exec_desc = executable_desc
276	        self.run_spec = executable_desc["runSpec"]
277	        self.job_desc = job_desc
278	        self.stage = self.job_desc.get("function", "main")
279	        self.logger = logger
280	
281	        self.dep_groups = []
282	        for dep in itertools.chain(self._get_local_bundled_dependencies(),
283	                                   self.run_spec.get("execDepends", []),
284	                                   self.run_spec.get("dependencies", [])):
285	            self._validate_dependency(dep)
286	
287	            dep_type = self._get_dependency_type(dep)
288	
289	            # Ignore dx-toolkit and jq from execDepends. They do not play nice
290	            if dep["name"] in ("dx-toolkit", "jq", "python-argcomplete") and dep_type == "apt":
291	                continue
292	
293	            if "stages" in dep and self.stage not in dep["stages"]:
294	                self.log("Skipping dependency {} because it is inactive in stage (function) {}".format(dep["name"],
295	                                                                                                       self.stage))
296	                continue
297	
298	
299	            if len(self.dep_groups) == 0 or self.dep_groups[-1]["type"] != dep_type or dep_type not in self.group_pms:
300	                self.dep_groups.append({"type": dep_type, "deps": [], "index": len(self.dep_groups)})
301	            self.dep_groups[-1]["deps"].append(dep)
302	
303	    def _get_local_bundled_dependencies(self):
304	        bundled_depends_by_region = self.run_spec.get("bundledDependsByRegion")
305	        if bundled_depends_by_region is None:
306	            return self.run_spec.get("bundledDepends", [])
307	        else:
308	            # Resolve the local bundled dependencies for this job.
309	            job_region = self.job_desc["region"]
310	            return bundled_depends_by_region[job_region]
311	
312	    def log(self, message):
313	        if self.logger:
314	            self.logger.info(message)
315	        else:
316	            print(message)
317	
318	    def generate_shellcode(self, dep_group):
319	        base_apt_shellcode = "export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends -o Dpkg::Options::=\"--force-confdef\" -o Dpkg::Options::=\"--force-confold\" {p}"
320	        dx_apt_update_shellcode = "apt-get update -o Dir::Etc::sourcelist=sources.list.d/nucleus.list -o Dir::Etc::sourceparts=- -o APT::Get::List-Cleanup=0"
321	        apt_err_msg = "APT failed, retrying with full update against official package repository"
322	        apt_shellcode_template = "({dx_upd} && {inst}) || (echo {e}; apt-get update && {inst})"
323	        apt_shellcode = apt_shellcode_template.format(dx_upd=dx_apt_update_shellcode,
324	                                                      inst=base_apt_shellcode,
325	                                                      e=apt_err_msg)
326	        def make_pm_atoms(packages, version_separator="="):
327	            package_atoms = (p["name"] + (version_separator+p["version"] if "version" in p else "") for p in packages)
328	            return " ".join(map(str, package_atoms))
329	
330	        dep_type, packages = dep_group["type"], dep_group["deps"]
331	        if dep_type == "apt":
332	            return apt_shellcode.format(p=make_pm_atoms(packages))
333	        elif dep_type == "pip":
334	            return "pip install --upgrade " + make_pm_atoms(packages, version_separator="==")
335	        elif dep_type == "pip3":
336	            return "pip3 install --upgrade " + make_pm_atoms(packages, version_separator="==")
337	        elif dep_type == "gem":
338	            commands = []
339	            for p in packages:
340	                commands.append("gem install " + p["name"])
341	                if "version" in p:
342	                    commands[-1] += " --version " + p["version"]
343	            return " && ".join(map(str, commands))
344	        elif dep_type == "cpan":
345	            return "cpanm --notest " + make_pm_atoms(packages, version_separator="~")
346	        elif dep_type == "cran":
347	            repo = "http://cloud.r-project.org"
348	            r_preamble = "die <- function() { q(status=1) }; options(error=die); options(warn=2);"
349	            r_preamble += 'r <- getOption("repos"); r["CRAN"] = "{repo}"; options(repos=r)'.format(repo=repo)
350	            r_cmd_template = "R -e '{preamble}; {cmd}'"
351	            bootstrap_cmd = 'install.packages("devtools")'
352	            commands = []
353	            for package in packages:
354	                if "version" in package:
355	                    cmd = 'require(devtools); install_version("{name}", version="{version}")'.format(**package)
356	                else:
357	                    cmd = 'install.packages("{}")'.format(package["name"])
358	                commands.append(r_cmd_template.format(preamble=r_preamble, cmd=cmd))
359	            if any("require(devtools)" in cmd for cmd in commands):
360	                commands.insert(0, r_cmd_template.format(preamble=r_preamble, cmd=bootstrap_cmd))
361	            return " && ".join(commands)
362	        elif dep_type == "git":
363	            commands = ["apt-get install --yes git make", "export GIT_SSH=dx-git-ssh-helper"]
364	            for dep in packages:
365	                subcommands = []
366	                build_dir = str(dep.get("destdir", "$(mktemp -d)"))
367	                subcommands.append("mkdir -p %s" % build_dir)
368	                subcommands.append("cd %s" % build_dir)
369	                subcommands.append("git clone " + str(dep["url"]))
370	                subdir = re.search("([^\/]+)$", str(dep["url"])).group(1)
371	                if subdir.endswith(".git"):
372	                    subdir = subdir[:-len(".git")]
373	                subcommands.append("cd '%s'" % subdir)
374	                if "tag" in dep:
375	                    subcommands.append("git checkout " + str(dep["tag"]))
376	                if "build_commands" in dep:
377	                    subcommands.append(str(dep["build_commands"]))
378	                commands.append("(" + " && ".join(subcommands) + ")")
379	            return " && ".join(commands)
380	        else:
381	            raise DXExecDependencyError("Package manager type {pm} not supported".format(pm=dep_type))
382	
383	    def run(self, cmd, log_fh=None):
384	        subprocess.check_call(cmd, shell=True, stdout=log_fh, stderr=log_fh)
385	
386	    def _install_dep_group(self, dep_group):
387	        self.log("Installing {} packages {}".format(dep_group["type"],
388	                                                    ", ".join(dep["name"] for dep in dep_group["deps"])))
389	        cmd = self.generate_shellcode(dep_group)
390	        log_filename = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "dx_{type}_install_{index}.log".format(**dep_group))
391	
392	        try:
393	            with open(log_filename, "w") as fh:
394	                self.run(cmd, log_fh=fh)
395	        except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
396	            with open(log_filename) as fh:
397	                sys.stdout.write(fh.read())
398	            raise DXExecDependencyError("Error while installing {type} packages {deps}".format(**dep_group))
399	
400	    def _install_dep_bundle(self, bundle):
401	        if bundle["id"].get("$dnanexus_link", "").startswith("file-"):
402	            self.log("Downloading bundled file {name}".format(**bundle))
403	            try:
404	                dxpy.download_dxfile(bundle["id"], bundle["name"], project=dxpy.WORKSPACE_ID)
405	            except dxpy.exceptions.ResourceNotFound:
406	                dxpy.download_dxfile(bundle["id"], bundle["name"])
407	            self.run("dx-unpack {}".format(shlex.quote(bundle["name"])))
408	        else:
409	            self.log('Skipping bundled dependency "{name}" because it does not refer to a file'.format(**bundle))
410	
411	    def install(self):
412	        for dep_group in self.dep_groups:
413	            if dep_group["type"] == "bundle":
414	                self._install_dep_bundle(dep_group["deps"][0])
415	            else:
416	                self._install_dep_group(dep_group)
417	
418	    def _validate_dependency(self, dep):
419	        if "name" not in dep:
420	            raise DXExecDependencyError('Expected field "name" to be present in execution dependency "{}"'.format(dep))
421	        elif dep.get("package_manager") == "git" and "url" not in dep:
422	            raise DXExecDependencyError('Execution dependency "{}" does not have a "url" field'.format(dep))
423	
424	    def _get_dependency_type(self, dep):
425	        if "id" in dep:
426	            return "bundle"
427	        else:
428	            return dep.get("package_manager", "apt")

17	'''
18	This module provides support for file download and upload. It calculates the
19	   location of the input and output directories. It also has a utility for parsing
20	   the job input file ('job_input.json').
21	
22	We use the following shorthands
23	   <idir> == input directory     $HOME/in
24	   <odir> == output directory    $HOME/out
25	
26	A simple example of the job input, when run locally, is:
27	
28	{
29	    "seq2": {
30	        "$dnanexus_link": {
31	            "project": "project-1111",
32	            "id": "file-1111"
33	        }
34	    },
35	    "seq1": {
36	        "$dnanexus_link": {
37	            "project": "project-2222",
38	            "id": "file-2222"
39	        }
40	    }
41	    "blast_args": "",
42	    "evalue": 0.01
43	}
44	
45	The first two elements are files {seq1, seq2}, the other elements are
46	{blast_args, evalue}. The files for seq1,seq2 should be saved into:
47	<idir>/seq1/<filename>
48	<idir>/seq2/<filename>
49	
50	An example for a shell command that would create these arguments is:
51	    $ dx run coolapp -iseq1=NC_000868.fasta -iseq2=NC_001422.fasta
52	It would run an app named "coolapp", with file arguments for seq1 and seq2. Both NC_*
53	files should be the names of files in a DNAnexus project (and should be resolved to their
54	file IDs by dx). Subsequently, after dx-download-all-inputs is run,
55	file seq1 should appear in the execution environment at path:
56	    <idir>/seq1/NC_000868.fasta
57	
58	File Arrays
59	
60	{
61	    "reads": [{
62	        "$dnanexus_link": {
63	            "project": "project-3333",
64	            "id": "file-3333"
65	        }
66	    },
67	    {
68	        "$dnanexus_link": {
69	            "project": "project-4444",
70	            "id": "file-4444"
71	        }
72	    }]
73	}
74	
75	This is a file array with two files. Running a command like this:
76	    $ dx run coolapp -ireads=A.fastq -ireads=B.fasta
77	will download into the execution environment:
78	<idir>/reads/A.fastq
79	             B.fastq
80	
81	'''

178	def make_unix_filename(fname):
179	    """
180	    :param fname: the basename of a file (e.g., xxx in /zzz/yyy/xxx).
181	    :returns: a valid unix filename
182	    :rtype: string
183	    :raises: DXError if the filename is invalid on a Unix system
184	
185	    The problem being solved here is that *fname* is a python string, it
186	    may contain characters that are invalid for a file name. We replace all the slashes with %2F.
187	    Another issue, is that the user may choose an invalid name. Since we focus
188	    on Unix systems, the only possibilies are "." and "..".
189	    """
190	    # sanity check for filenames
191	    bad_filenames = [".", ".."]
192	    if fname in bad_filenames:
193	        raise DXError("Invalid filename {}".format(fname))
194	    return fname.replace('/', '%2F')

202	def get_job_input_filenames(job_input_file):
203	    """Extract list of files, returns a set of directories to create, and
204	    a set of files, with sources and destinations. The paths created are
205	    relative to the input directory.
206	
207	    Note: we go through file names inside arrays, and create a
208	    separate subdirectory for each. This avoids clobbering files when
209	    duplicate filenames appear in an array.
210	    """
211	    def get_input_hash():
212	        with open(job_input_file) as fh:
213	            job_input = json.load(fh)
214	            return job_input
215	    job_input = get_input_hash()
216	
217	    files = collections.defaultdict(list)  # dictionary, with empty lists as default elements
218	    dirs = []  # directories to create under <idir>
219	
220	    # Local function for adding a file to the list of files to be created
221	    # for example:
222	    #    iname == "seq1"
223	    #    subdir == "015"
224	    #    value == { "$dnanexus_link": {
225	    #       "project": "project-BKJfY1j0b06Z4y8PX8bQ094f",
226	    #       "id": "file-BKQGkgQ0b06xG5560GGQ001B"
227	    #    }
228	    # will create a record describing that the file should
229	    # be downloaded into seq1/015/<filename>
230	    def add_file(iname, subdir, value):
231	        if not dxpy.is_dxlink(value):
232	            return
233	        handler = dxpy.get_handler(value)
234	        if not isinstance(handler, dxpy.DXFile):
235	            return
236	        filename = make_unix_filename(handler.name)
237	        trg_dir = iname
238	        if subdir is not None:
239	            trg_dir = os.path.join(trg_dir, subdir)
240	        files[iname].append({'trg_fname': os.path.join(trg_dir, filename),
241	                             'handler': handler,
242	                             'src_file_id': handler.id})
243	        dirs.append(trg_dir)
244	
245	    # An array of inputs, for a single key. A directory
246	    # will be created per array entry. For example, if the input key is
247	    # FOO, and the inputs are {A, B, C}.vcf then, the directory structure
248	    # will be:
249	    #   <idir>/FOO/00/A.vcf
250	    #   <idir>/FOO/01/B.vcf
251	    #   <idir>/FOO/02/C.vcf
252	    def add_file_array(input_name, links):
253	        num_files = len(links)
254	        if num_files == 0:
255	            return
256	        num_digits = len(str(num_files - 1))
257	        dirs.append(input_name)
258	        for i, link in enumerate(links):
259	            subdir = str(i).zfill(num_digits)
260	            add_file(input_name, subdir, link)
261	
262	    for input_name, value in list(job_input.items()):
263	        if isinstance(value, list):
264	            # This is a file array
265	            add_file_array(input_name, value)
266	        else:
267	            add_file(input_name, None, value)
268	
269	    ## create a dictionary of the all non-file elements
270	    rest_hash = {key: val for key, val in list(job_input.items()) if key not in files}
271	    return dirs, files, rest_hash
